mainTopic: Measuring the תחום שבת across valleys and hills: spanning, piercing, and the lenient rules for surveyors
overview: This amud continues the rules for measuring the תחום שבת when the path crosses a valley or a hill. If a valley's wall is sheer, so that a plumb line drops straight down, the measurer measures the width properly. רב יוסף allows spanning a valley up to two thousand אמות deep. אביי objects from a ברייתא that says one hundred, and the גמרא answers that רב יוסף follows אחרים. In a second version, רב יוסף allows spanning even beyond two thousand. The גמרא explains that he is speaking of a vertical wall, and אבימי defines 'vertical' as a slope of less than four אמות. רבא, in two versions, explains which hills are spanned and which are measured or estimated. רב כהנא explains why the measurer may not step outside the תחום. A ברייתא describes the 'piercing' method (קידור), which is not used for עגלה ערופה or ערי מקלט. A new משנה then rules that only an expert measures, that the larger measurement is followed, and that even an עבד or שפחה is believed, because the תחום rules are meant to be lenient.

steps.title: When the valley wall is steep, measure it properly
steps.stepSummary: This is the closing clause of the previous teaching. If a plumb line can drop straight down along the valley wall, the measurer measures the valley properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if a plumb line drops straight down alongside it, he measures it with a proper measurement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a rule it began on the previous amud. A steep, sheer valley wall is treated differently from a gentle slope.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that a measurer who reaches a valley may 'swallow' it, meaning he stretches the rope across it. This clause adds a qualification. If the wall is so steep that a plumb line hangs straight down beside it, he measures the width properly, without counting the walls (following Sefaria's explanation).

keyTerms.meaning: A plumb line: a string with a weight that hangs straight down
Drops straight down alongside it, meaning the wall is sheer

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the END of a statement that began on the previous amud. It is not a brand-new teaching, so don't look for its opening here.

phrases.english: But if a plumb line drops straight down alongside it —
phrases.notes: The valley wall is steep or sheer

phrases.english: he measures it with a proper measurement.
phrases.notes: He measures the width at the bottom, without counting the walls.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the qualification of the משנה's rule about valleys, which began on the previous amud
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A valley with a sheer wall, where a plumb line drops straight down, is measured properly rather than handled in the ordinary way.

steps.title: How deep can the valley be?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the maximum depth of a valley that may still be spanned.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how deep may the valley be?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question. The answer comes in the very next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave a width limit of fifty אמות for spanning a valley but said nothing about depth. The גמרא wants to know whether a very deep valley can still be 'swallowed' by the rope.

phrases.english: And how deep may the valley be?
phrases.notes: That is, how deep may it be and still be spanned

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the steepness of the wall to the depth of the valley
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The maximum depth at which a valley up to fifty אמות wide can still be spanned

steps.title: רב יוסף: up to two thousand
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that a valley up to two thousand אמות deep may be spanned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: two thousand.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question with a number: two thousand אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב יוסף, a valley up to two thousand אמות deep (and up to fifty wide) is spanned with the rope. If it is deeper than that, the slope must be measured as well.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, the head of the academy at פומבדיתא

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: two thousand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the depth question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A valley may be spanned if it is up to two thousand אמות deep.

steps.title: אביי objects from a ברייתא that says one hundred
steps.stepSummary: אביי cites a ברייתא that permits spanning only up to one hundred אמות deep, which contradicts רב יוסף's two thousand.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged him: 'If it is a hundred deep and fifty wide, he spans it. And if not, he does not span it!'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's answer by quoting a ברייתא with a much smaller depth limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a valley up to one hundred deep and fifty wide may be spanned, and otherwise it may not. That directly contradicts רב יוסף's limit of two thousand, so how could he rule that way?

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him, using a תנאי source
אביי, the student and colleague of רב יוסף
He 'swallows' it: spans it with the measuring rope without measuring its slopes

phrases.english: Abaye challenged him:
phrases.notes: אביי is bringing a question from a ברייתא.

phrases.english: If it is a hundred deep and fifty wide — he spans it.
And if not — he does not span it?
phrases.notes: The unspoken question: so how can רב יוסף say two thousand?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's answer
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's depth limit of two thousand
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא limits spanning to one hundred deep, so a limit of two thousand contradicts a תנאי source.

steps.title: רב יוסף follows אחרים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב יוסף holds like אחרים, who permit spanning even at two thousand deep.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like אחרים, as it was taught in a ברייתא: אחרים say, 'Even if it is two thousand deep and fifty wide, he spans it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב יוסף by showing that his view matches another תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא אביי quoted is only one opinion, the תנא קמא. A different ברייתא records אחרים allowing spanning up to two thousand deep. רב יוסף simply ruled like them, so there is no real contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Others': an unnamed תנא or group of תנאים (often identified as רבי מאיר)
As it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: There is a מחלוקת תנאים on depth: the תנא קמא says one hundred, and אחרים say two thousand. In the first version, רב יוסף follows אחרים.

phrases.english: He spoke in accordance with Acherim,
as it was taught: Acherim say:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ עָמוֹק אַלְפַּיִם וְרוֹחַב חֲמִשִּׁים — מַבְלִיעוֹ.
phrases.english: Even if it is two thousand deep and fifty wide — he spans it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves אביי's objection
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying a dispute between תנאים: the אמורא follows the other opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יוסף contradicts the only ברייתא on the subject.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is the תנא קמא's view, and רב יוסף follows אחרים.

steps.title: Second version: even more than two thousand
steps.stepSummary: An alternate tradition (איכא דאמרי) records רב יוסף permitting spanning even when the valley is deeper than two thousand.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say that רב יוסף said: even more than two thousand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different report of what רב יוסף said. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, רב יוסף sets no depth limit at all. Any depth may be spanned. That goes beyond even the view of אחרים.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say: introduces an alternate version of a tradition

steps.confusionAlert: This does not continue the previous back-and-forth. It is a completely different version of רב יוסף's statement, and it replaces 'two thousand' with 'even more than two thousand.'

phrases.english: Some say: Rav Yosef said:
Even more than two thousand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different version of רב יוסף's answer from step 3
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A valley may be spanned even if it is deeper than two thousand אמות.

steps.title: Whose view is that? Neither תנא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the second version, since it matches neither the תנא קמא nor אחרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does this follow? Not the תנא קמא's, and not אחרים'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second version by pointing out that no תנא holds it. The answer is not here; it comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא allows only one hundred deep, and אחרים allow up to two thousand. Saying 'more than two thousand' exceeds both. So it seems רב יוסף has no תנאי source behind him.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, anonymous תנא of a ברייתא

phrases.english: In accordance with whom?
It is not like the first tanna and not like Acherim!

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן? דְּלָא כְּתַנָּא קַמָּא וְלָא כַּאֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the alternate version in step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The second version of רב יוסף's statement (even more than two thousand)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both known תנאים set a limit, one hundred or two thousand, so no limit at all contradicts both of them.

steps.title: Sheer walls versus sloped walls
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the difficulty from step 7. The תנאים discuss a sloped valley wall. רב יוסף discusses a sheer vertical wall, which may be spanned even when it is deeper than two thousand אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the plumb line does not drop straight down. Here, the plumb line does drop straight down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of how רב יוסף could allow spanning a valley deeper than two thousand. It explains that he is talking about a different kind of valley than the תנאים are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא (both the תנא קמא and אחרים) deals with a valley whose walls slope, so there is a reason to measure the slope. רב יוסף deals with a valley whose walls go straight down like a plumb line. A wall like that cannot really be measured, so it is spanned no matter how deep it is. Since the cases are different, nobody is contradicting anybody.

keyTerms.meaning: There: the case in the other source (here, the ברייתא)
Here: the case we are discussing (רב יוסף's statement)
A plumb line, a weighted string that hangs perfectly straight down

steps.confusionAlert: 'Plumb line drops straight down' does not mean the valley is shallow. It means the wall is vertical. That is exactly why even a very deep valley may be spanned.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key distinction for the rest of the סוגיא. A vertical drop is simply spanned, while a sloped drop involves real measurement rules.

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם — שֶׁאֵין חוּט הַמִּשְׁקוֹלֶת יוֹרֵד כְּנֶגְדּוֹ.
phrases.english: There, it is where a plumb line does not drop straight down opposite it.
phrases.notes: Refers to the ברייתא's case of a sloped wall.

phrases.english: Here, it is where a plumb line drops straight down opposite it.
phrases.notes: Refers to רב יוסף's case of a vertical wall.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם — שֶׁאֵין חוּט הַמִּשְׁקוֹלֶת יוֹרֵד כְּנֶגְדּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 by splitting the cases apart.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case distinction (אוקימתא): the sources address different physical situations
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed רב יוסף and the ברייתא were talking about the same kind of valley, so he seemed to fit neither the תנא קמא nor אחרים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about sloped walls and רב יוסף is about vertical walls. A vertical valley is spanned at any depth.

steps.title: How much slope still counts as vertical
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how far the wall may slope out and still be treated as 'the plumb line drops straight down'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And regarding 'the plumb line does not drop straight down': up to how much?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the גמרא has introduced the idea of a vertical wall, it asks for the exact measurement. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In real life, almost no wall is perfectly vertical. So the גמרא needs a limit: how much outward slope is allowed before the wall stops counting as vertical and has to be measured as a slope?

keyTerms.meaning: And when (introduces the case being asked about)
Up to how much? (asks for a measurement or limit)

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי אֵין חוּט הַמִּשְׁקוֹלֶת יוֹרֵד כְּנֶגְדּוֹ,
phrases.english: And when the plumb line does not drop straight down opposite it,
up to how much?
phrases.notes: How far may the bottom extend out from the top?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אֵין חוּט הַמִּשְׁקוֹלֶת יוֹרֵד כְּנֶגְדּוֹ, עַד כַּמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a precise definition of the distinction made in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The maximum amount of outward slope that still counts as a 'vertical' wall.

steps.title: אבימי sets the limit at four
steps.stepSummary: אבימי answers that the limit is four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבימי said: four.
steps.whatsHappening: אבימי gives the measurement the גמרא asked for: four אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the bottom of the valley lies less than four אמות of the top edge, the wall is treated like a vertical drop. If it lies four אמות or more out, the wall is a slope and must be measured.

phrases.english: Avimi said: Four (cubits).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A slope of up to four אמות still counts as a vertical wall.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the figure of four
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר יחזקאל taught the same figure of four in a ברייתא, which supports אבימי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so too רמי בר יחזקאל taught: four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a taught source that says the same number, backing up אבימי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'וכן תני' tells us that a ברייתא tradition agrees with the אמורא. This means אבימי's number is not just his own opinion; it matches an older teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught, meaning he recited a ברייתא
רמי בר יחזקאל, a teacher of ברייתות

steps.whatToRemember: A vertical valley wall (a slope of less than four אמות) is spanned at any depth. A sloped valley follows the ברייתא's limits.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן תָּנֵי רָמֵי בַּר יְחֶזְקֵאל: אַרְבַּע.
phrases.english: And similarly Rami bar Yeḥezkel taught: Four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 10.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא taught by רמי בר יחזקאל

steps.title: The משנה's rule about reaching a hill
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: when measuring the תחום and reaching a hill, one spans it and then resumes measuring.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he reached a hill, he spans it and returns to his measurement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה about hills. It quotes the line so it can comment on it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person measuring the תחום does not climb up and down the hill with the rope. He treats the hill as if it were flat ground, 'swallowing' it, and then continues measuring on the far side.

keyTerms.meaning: He 'swallows' it: spans it as if it were not there

phrases.english: If he reached a hill,
he spans it and returns to his measurement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: hills instead of valleys.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hill in the measuring path is spanned, and measurement resumes after it.

steps.title: רבא limits the rule to steep hills
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the משנה's spanning rule applies only to a steep hill, one rising ten טפחים within four אמות. A gentler hill, rising ten within five, must be measured properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: They taught this only about a hill that rises ten within four. But a hill that rises ten within five must be measured properly.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא narrows the משנה's rule. Only steep hills get spanned, and gentle hills are measured.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A steep hill (ten טפחים of height in four אמות of length) is too hard to measure across, so it is spanned. A gentler hill (ten in five) is easy enough to walk with the rope, so the measurer must measure it normally.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught (this rule) in the case of: a limiting formula
That rises or gathers up: describes the steepness of the slope
He measures it properly, without skipping it

phrases.english: Rava said:
They taught this only regarding a hill
that rises ten (handbreadths) within four (cubits),

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּהַר הַמִּתְלַקֵּט עֲשָׂרָה מִתּוֹךְ חָמֵשׁ —
phrases.english: but regarding a hill that rises ten within five,
he measures it properly.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בְּהַר הַמִּתְלַקֵּט עֲשָׂרָה מִתּוֹךְ אַרְבַּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies the משנה quoted in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Span a hill rising ten within four. Measure properly a hill rising ten within five.

steps.title: A more lenient version of רבא
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן reports רבא differently. The משנה's spanning rule applies even to a gentler hill (ten within five). A steeper hill (ten within four) is simply estimated, and the measurer moves on.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן taught it leniently. רבא said: They taught this only about a hill rising ten within five. But a hill rising ten within four, he estimates it and goes on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, more lenient version of רבא's statement. In this version, even gentle hills are spanned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, a gentle hill (ten within five) had to be measured. In this version, that same hill is spanned, which is the משנה's rule. A steep hill (ten within four) does not even need careful spanning; the measurer just estimates it and continues. Because both kinds of hills are treated more leniently than in the first version, this version is called לקולא.

keyTerms.meaning: רב הונא, son of רב נתן
Teaches it in the lenient way: an alternate version
And goes on his way: continues measuring past it

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions use the same numbers (four and five), but they assign them differently. In version one, ten within five means 'measure'. In version two, ten within five means 'span' and ten within four means 'just estimate'.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of רבא. Strict version: a steep hill is spanned and a gentle hill is measured. Lenient version: a gentle hill is spanned and a steep hill is just estimated.

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן מַתְנֵי לְקוּלָּא.
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Natan teaches it leniently.
Rava said:
They taught this only regarding a hill
that rises ten within five,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּהַר הַמִּתְלַקֵּט עֲשָׂרָה מִתּוֹךְ אַרְבַּע —
phrases.english: but regarding a hill that rises ten within four,
he estimates it and goes on his way.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן מַתְנֵי לְקוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents an alternate, more lenient tradition of רבא's statement in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hill rising ten within five is spanned. A hill rising ten within four is estimated, and the measurer moves on.

steps.title: Why may the measurer not go past the תחום?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's condition that the person spanning a hill must not go out past the תחום, and asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'As long as he does not go outside the תחום.' What is the reason for this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes one more line from the משנה and asks why that condition exists. This sets up רב כהנא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a hill or valley is narrow enough for the rope to reach across, the measurer may span it, meaning he skips over it. The משנה adds a condition: while doing this, he may not walk outside the תחום. The גמרא wants to know why, since he is only measuring.

phrases.english: Provided that he does not go out beyond the limit.
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה after the discussion of רבא's two versions and takes up the next clause.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the measurer may not step outside the תחום while spanning.

steps.title: People might think the תחום reaches there
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא explains that this is a rabbinic decree, so that onlookers do not think the measured תחום extends to wherever they see him standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: It is a decree, so that people will not say, 'The measurement of the תחום reaches up to here.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers the question. People who see the measurer outside the תחום could think the boundary really reaches that spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows this man is measuring the תחום. If they see him standing somewhere past the real limit, they will assume the limit reaches that point and will walk there on שבת. The חכמים prevented this misunderstanding by keeping him inside the limit.

keyTerms.meaning: A protective decree of the חכמים
Lest people say (out of a misunderstanding)
The measurement of the Shabbat limits

steps.whatToRemember: The measurer must stay inside the תחום so that onlookers do not think the boundary extends to where they see him.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
It is a decree, lest people say
the measurement of the limits comes up to here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a rabbinic decree against the mistaken impression that the תחום extends to wherever the measurer is seen.

steps.title: How the 'piercing' method works
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case where the hill cannot be spanned and brings a ברייתא describing קידור. The lower person holds the rope at his heart and the upper person holds it at his feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If he cannot span it,' then he 'pierces' it. The חכמים taught: How do we pierce? The lower person holds the rope at the level of his heart, and the upper person holds it at the level of his feet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, about a hill too wide to span. It brings a ברייתא that explains how the 'piercing' method is done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קידור is described as if the measurers were drilling straight through the hill. Two people climb the slope one above the other. The lower one raises the rope to his heart and the upper one keeps it at his feet, so the rope stays roughly level. This way only the flat, horizontal distance is counted, not the extra length of the slope.

keyTerms.meaning: To span it, measuring across the hill or valley as if it were not there
'Piercing': measuring a slope horizontally, as if drilling through it

steps.confusionAlert: Nobody actually digs into the hill. 'Piercing' is only a picture: the rope is held level, as if it ran straight through the slope.

phrases.english: If he cannot span it.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה; it continues 'he pierces it.'

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
How does one pierce?
The lower one holds it opposite his heart,
the upper one holds it opposite his feet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the spanning rule to the backup method used when spanning is impossible.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In קידור the rope is held level, with the lower person holding it at his heart and the upper person at his feet.

steps.title: The piercing rope must be four אמות
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports a tradition that קידור may be done only with a rope four אמות long.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We have a tradition that one may pierce only with a rope of four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a detail to the piercing method: the rope must be short, only four אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The method only works if the rope stays level between the two people. A short rope means short steps along the slope, which keeps the measurement close to the true horizontal distance. With a long rope it would be hard to hold the rope level.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
We hold by tradition that one may not pierce
except with a rope of four cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְקִיטִינַן אֵין מְקַדְּרִין אֶלָּא בְּחֶבֶל שֶׁל אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a detail about the rope's length to the method described in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קידור is done only with a four-אמה rope.

steps.title: No piercing for עגלה ערופה or ערי מקלט
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, reports a tradition that קידור is not used when measuring for עגלה ערופה or ערי מקלט, because those measurements are from the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: We have a tradition that we do not pierce for עגלה ערופה or for ערי מקלט, because they are from the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new tradition limits where the piercing shortcut may be used. It works for the תחום, but not for two measurements that the תורה itself commands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spanning and piercing are allowed shortcuts for measuring the תחום. For עגלה ערופה (finding which city is closest to a murder victim) and ערי מקלט (the boundaries that protect an accidental killer), the measurement is a law of the תורה. So these shortcuts are not used there, and the area must be measured fully, as if it were flat.

keyTerms.meaning: The beheaded calf brought when a murder victim is found and the killer is unknown
Cities of refuge for an accidental killer

steps.whatToRemember: The 'piercing' method is allowed for תחום שבת but not for the דאורייתא measurements of עגלה ערופה and ערי מקלט.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that measuring shortcuts depend on the level of the law. דאורייתא measurements require full measuring.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
(We hold by tradition that) one may not pierce
neither for the beheaded calf
nor for cities of refuge,
because they are from the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מְקַדְּרִין לֹא בְּעֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה וְלֹא בְּעָרֵי מִקְלָט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the method and its rope length are defined, this step limits where the method may be used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קידור is not used for עגלה ערופה or ערי מקלט, because those measurements are דאורייתא.

steps.title: Only an expert may measure
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that the תחום may be measured only by an expert surveyor.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: We measure only through an expert.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. Its first rule is that only a skilled surveyor may measure the תחום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Measuring the תחום involves rope tricks like spanning and piercing, which an ordinary person could get wrong. So the משנה requires an expert to do it.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One may measure only with an expert.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. The topic of measuring the תחום continues.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only an expert surveyor may measure the תחום.

steps.title: When measurements conflict, follow the larger one
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if the expert's measurement came out larger in one place and smaller in another, or larger for one person and smaller for another, we follow the larger measurement.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he made it bigger in one place and smaller in another place, we listen to the place where he made it bigger. If he made it bigger for one and smaller for another, we listen to the bigger one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with what to do when measurements do not match. In both cases the answer is the same: follow the bigger measurement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one measurement shows a larger area, the smaller one probably came from a measuring error, such as a rope that was pulled loosely or not straight. So the larger result is trusted. The משנה gives two versions of this: two different places, and two different people.
steps.whatToRemember: When two measurements of the תחום conflict, we follow the larger one.

phrases.english: If he extended it in one place,
and reduced it in another place,
we listen to the place where he extended.
If he extended it for one and reduced it for another,
we listen to the larger one.

steps.triggerLanguage: רִיבָּה לְמָקוֹם אֶחָד וּמִיעֵט לְמָקוֹם אַחֵר שׁוֹמְעִין לִמְקוֹם שֶׁרִיבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the new משנה with the rule for conflicting measurements.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When measurements conflict, we follow the larger one.

steps.title: Even an עבד or שפחה is believed about the תחום שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that even an עבד or a שפחה is trusted to say where the תחום שבת ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even a slave, even a maidservant, are believed to say: 'The תחום שבת reaches up to here.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one more leniency: even people who are usually not accepted as witnesses are believed when they report where the תחום ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually an עבד or a שפחה cannot testify. Here the משנה relaxes that rule and accepts their simple report about the boundary. This continues the lenient direction of Step 21, where we follow the larger measurement.

keyTerms.meaning: A (non-Jewish, Canaanite) slave owned by a Jew. Normally not a valid witness.
A (non-Jewish, Canaanite) maidservant. Normally not a valid witness.
The Shabbat boundary, 2,000 אמות beyond one's place, which one may not walk past

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a general rule that slaves are valid witnesses. They are believed only here, because the laws of תחומין are treated leniently.

phrases.english: And even a slave, even a maidservant
phrases.notes: People who are normally not valid witnesses

phrases.english: are believed to say
'Up to here is the Shabbat boundary.'
phrases.notes: They report where the 2,000 אמות end

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another leniency to the משנה's rules about measuring the תחום, following Step 21's rule to go by the larger measurement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עבד or a שפחה is believed to testify where the תחום שבת ends.

steps.title: The reason: the חכמים made boundary rules to be lenient
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains that חכמים gave the rules of תחומין to be lenient, not to be strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the חכמים did not say this matter (the rules of the תחום שבת) to be strict, but to be lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the reason behind its lenient rulings: the laws of measuring the תחום are meant to be applied leniently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 2,000-אמה limit is a rabbinic law (דרבנן), so when there is doubt we lean toward the lenient side. This one reason explains both rulings: following the larger measurement (Step 21) and believing an עבד or a שפחה (Step 22).

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic law (not from the Torah). The Shabbat boundary limit is treated this way here.

steps.whatToRemember: The rules of measuring the תחום שבת are applied leniently. So we follow the larger measurement, and we believe even an עבד or a שפחה about where the boundary is.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle ties together the משנה's rulings and explains why the גמרא treats doubts about תחומין with leniency.

phrases.english: because the Sages did not say the matter
phrases.notes: 'The matter' means the laws of the Shabbat boundary

phrases.english: to be strict, but rather to be lenient.
phrases.notes: So in doubtful cases we are lenient

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁלֹּא אָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים אֶת הַדָּבָר לְהַחֲמִיר אֶלָּא לְהָקֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the leniencies in Steps 21 and 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The laws of תחומין were given to be lenient, so doubts are resolved leniently.
